summary: Approve per-browser message-capable device grants through existing native person asks

replay.detail: No claim replay is required. Browser requests and device grants use the existing pairing and person-ask claim paths.

schema.detail: No database schema changes or data migration.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or digest changes; no coordinated member upgrade is required.

compatibility.detail: Existing native person asks render Approve and Deny answers without an app update. Browser approval requires an existing paired device with control.pairing and a native admission receipt from an answering member running this build or later; answers from older members fail closed. Browser grants receive web read scopes and control.messages only. Browser requests use a dedicated verifier for a 32-byte lowercase-hex request key, independent of legacy native challenge verification. The normal limited device-pairing scope list is unchanged.

downtime.detail: No additional startup work or expected interruption.

manual.detail: Browser pairing is disabled by default. Before enabling browser_pairing_login, update the answering members to this build or later; otherwise requests fail closed. Configure the owning person and browser_pairing_login in daemon configuration, matching the publisher's admitted tailnet login. Compare the display code with the browser before approving its five-minute request. Each publisher device may begin ten requests per five minutes, with at most three pending per login.

recovery.detail: No migration or additional swap-back restrictions. Browser grants expire after 30 days and can be revoked through existing device controls or by the browser itself.
